MALACAÑAN PALACE
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES
[ EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 22, March 17, 1936 ]
CONSTITUTING A COMMITTEE ON PENSIONS AND APPOINTING THE MEMBERS THEREOF
WHEREAS, reports have been received of the insolvent condition of the several pension systems of the
Government, necessitating that step be taken immediately to place these systems on a sound financial basis;
WHEREAS, from time to time legislation providing for retirement, gratuity, and pension payments has been
approved without discriminate regard for length of service rendered, for age of retirement and for the amounts
of benefit to be paid; and
WHEREAS, it is now deemed necessary to make provision for a general retirement law to relieve
superannuation in the positions of the public service with due regard to the interests of the Government and
the beneficiaries;
NOW, THEREFORE, I, MANUEL L. QUEZON, President of the Philippines, by virtue of the powers in me
vested by law, resolve to constitute, as I hereby constitute, a Committee on Pensions to be composed of the
Mr. Salvador Lagdameo, Chairman; Mr. Antonio Ramos, member; Mr. Celedonio Salvador, member; Dr.
Leoncio Lopez-Rizal, member; Maj. Hipolito Garma, member; Dr. Emeterio B. Roa, member; Dr. Luis R.
Salvosa, member and Secretary;
to make a survey of existing retirement, gratuity, and pension systems in effect in the Philippines, and to study
the advisability of continuing, modifying, amending, or abolishing any or all of the several pension systems
with due respect of the established rights of the beneficiaries, or to recommend the adoption of a general
retirement plan to cover the entire public service.
